clue.text: Pustule genetically modified? No help fiddling round that

indicators.note: fiddling with something means tinkering with it, so the letters before it get rearranged
the rearranged letters go round the thing just mentioned, enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the standard abbreviation, as in GM crops

explanation.surface: A worried note about a mutant pustule that no amount of tinkering will help.
explanation.definitionFit: A phlegmon is a spreading inflammation that forms pus, close kin to an abscess or boil.

clue.text: One's thick-bodied and hairy, almost killed in thrust

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the creature

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
one word is placed inside another

blocks.note: to thrust is to push
smote, past tense of smite, can mean struck dead

explanation.surface: A grim description of some hairy brute nearly killed in a lunge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's thick-bodied and hairy' reads like a slur on a person; it describes a moth.
explanation.definitionFit: The puss moth is a large furry moth with a stout body, so the description fits it.

clue.text: Short poem, endless claptrap king penned

penned means shut in, as in a pen, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: hokum is nonsense or claptrap
K is king in chess notation

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a royal's brief verse as endless nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: A hokku is the opening verse of a Japanese linked poem, essentially a haiku, a famously brief form.

clue.text: See me oil RR that's faulty? I'll deal with gear

definitions.note: the answer speaks in the first person

indicators.note: something faulty is out of order, so these letters must be put in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A mechanic asks to be called if a Rolls-Royce's oil is faulty, offering to fix its gearing.
explanation.walkthrough: RR is the Rolls-Royce badge, which makes 'gear' look like a car's gearbox; here it is horse tack.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorimer is a craftsman making bits, spurs and other metal fittings for horse harness.

clue.text: Cotton worker from north cutting finger badly? Not the first

done badly, the letters end up in the wrong order
a cut goes into something, so this letter sits inside the rest

the compass abbreviation

explanation.definitionFit: A ginner operates a cotton gin, the machine separating fibre from seeds.

clue.text: Multiplex, showing such as the Hydra

blocks.note: first meaning: having many parts or forms
second meaning: like the mythical serpent with many heads

explanation.walkthrough: 'Multiplex' suggests a cinema, but it is used in its sense of manifold; the Hydra grew new heads as fast as Hercules cut them off.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both something manifold and a beast with numerous heads like the Hydra.

clue.text: Nitro blasted core of igneous rock

the central letter of the seven

explanation.walkthrough: 'igneous rock' looks like one phrase, but only 'rock' defines; 'igneous' just supplies its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Norite is a coarse-grained igneous rock, a variety of gabbro.

clue.text: Birds to preserve, first to last

indicators.note: the opening letter is moved to the end of the word

blocks.note: to preserve is to save

explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs on to 'hung', making it look like the start of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Vifda is the Shetland word for beef or mutton hung and dried without salting.

clue.text: Aid to modern travel replacing kite etc

indicators.note: putting letters back in different places reorders them

blocks.note: taken as written

clue.text: Get aid with oil being mined for rosy mineral

clue.text: Grand foreign lady (with no trace of accent) very much withdrawn in Geneva

clue.text: Fancy fish tasted for supper
